text:
eng-incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING @oncall — embeddings service p95 latency > 800ms for 10m. KV-cache hit rate dropped to 18% (was ~85%). Increased retries and elevated error responses observed.

sara: I'm taking this.

lee: grabbing logs + cache stats now, are we sure it's the KV cache and not a model fallback?

sara: traces point to cache misses + eviction spikes around 23:04 UTC. a lot of 502s coming from embed-serving workers.

lee: quick check:
```
curl -s http://metrics.internal/caches/kv-cache/stats | jq .
# -> {"hit_rate":0.18, "evictions_per_min":320, "size_bytes":512000000}
```

tanvi: evictions at 320/min is huge — smells like TTL churn from a bad client pattern.

mike: any recent deploys?

sara: no deploys in the last 6h. only a config push to autoscaler ~8h ago.

juan: noticed a burst from client_id=box-ops-3 around the same time. could be a runaway job.

sara: temporarily added rate-limit rule on the edge for that client (applied).

lee: after the rate-limit, hit_rate climbed to ~46% in the following 5m :thumbsup: 

eng-incident-bot: NOTE: Alert suppressed for 15m per on-call mitigation.

sara: customer impact: paid Dedicated customers calling embeddings saw increased latency and ~0.4% error spike; we'll log this to an incident ticket.

tanvi: alert tuning suggestion — current alert fires on hit_rate < 40% for 5m which is noisy for short bursts. propose: hit_rate < 30% for 10m, and add eviction-rate alert when evictions_per_min > 200.

mike: +1. Also add a Grafana panel for evictions/sec and top-keys-by-eviction to the cache dashboard.

lee: mock panel created: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/cache-hitrates (temp link)

sara: opened incident RUN-5732 and a draft PR for alert changes: https://git.redwood.internal/ops/alerts/pulls/88

juan: mitigation: rolling increase cache max_items from 1.2M -> 1.8M on the pool (started).

sara: handoff planned in 30m to @oncall-cover. I'll monitor eviction rate and customer emails until then.

oncall-cover: thanks, I'll pick up after 19:30 UTC. what's the official runbook step for eviction spikes?

sara: runbook step 4: 'If evictions/sec > 100 for 10m: check top-10 keys, consider temp increase to cache size or apply client-level throttling.' pasting into thread.

mike: post-incident action list: [1] implement eviction-rate alert, [2] add TTL histogram panel, [3] investigate box-ops-3 client pattern, [4] evaluate soft-affinity/warming per-tenant caches.

tanvi: adding tasks to RUN-5732.

lee: also, we should suppress the p95 latency alert during planned cache-scaling/warmup windows to reduce noise — suggest suppression window 30m after any cache scaling op.

sara: agree. I'll update the alert config in the PR.

sara: statuspage update scheduled — will mark embeddings service as degraded and note ongoing mitigations :memo:

eng-incident-bot: INCIDENT RUN-5732 created; severity: P2.

sara: update: eviction_rate down to 18/min, hit_rate stable ~78%. rolling config changes completed. Leaving monitoring to @oncall-cover. Post-mortem scheduled tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

oncall-cover: ack, taking over. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
